title: Check your understanding: Storage Formats & Serialization

items.prompt: Why are columnar formats such as Apache Parquet vastly faster than row-oriented CSV files for analytical queries?
choices: Columnar formats encrypt all data using public keys by default
Columnar formats enable projection pushdown to load only requested columns, and exploit type homogeneity for high compression
Row stores cannot be read by multi-core processors
Columnar formats eliminate the need for an operating system file system
items.explain: Columnar layouts group identical attribute types contiguously, allowing engines to read only the columns needed by a query and achieve high compression via dictionary and run-length encoding.

items.prompt: How does predicate pushdown operate in Apache Parquet to accelerate filtered queries?
choices: It decompresses all row groups sequentially and checks every row in Python
It uses min/max column metadata stored in row group headers to skip entire blocks from disk if they cannot match the filter condition
It deletes unmatched rows permanently from the storage drive
It re-encodes numbers into ASCII strings for faster regular expression matching
items.explain: Row group headers contain min, max, and null count statistics. If a filter predicate cannot be satisfied within those bounds, the entire row group is skipped without reading it from disk.

items.prompt: Which format is specifically designed for high-dimensional scientific tensors and multidimensional array slicing (e.g. physics simulations and climate models)?
items.explain: HDF5 is designed to store large, multidimensional numerical arrays in hierarchical groups with chunking and native binary compression.

items.prompt: In an uncompressed row-oriented format, calculating the average of a single numeric column requires reading all other unused column bytes on that row from disk.
items.explain: Because row-oriented stores pack all attributes of a tuple contiguously, reading one column requires scanning through the entire physical row.

items.prompt: Explain how dictionary encoding and run-length encoding (RLE) combine to compress low-cardinality categorical data.
items.rubric: Dictionary replaces long strings with short integer tokens; RLE replaces consecutive duplicate tokens with (token, count) pairs.
items.sample_answer: Dictionary encoding replaces repetitive string values with small integer IDs, and run-length encoding collapses consecutive identical IDs into compact (value, count) pairs.
